analysis: What changed vs the 4:00 AM brief: the overnight story firmed up rather than changed. Futures drifted slightly deeper (Nasdaq 100 -2.33% vs -2.19%, S&P 500 -1.04% vs -0.97%) while the Dow stayed near flat, and the morning's one genuinely fresh print — Exxon and Chevron both beating on a refining surge — confirmed the rotation offset rather than breaking it: XOM +2%, CVX +1% premarket. The chip sympathy trade is now quantified: AMD -8.6%, Broadcom -3.8%, Nvidia -2.9% on Intel's PC warning, with Dell and HP falling too, so Intel's guide is a sector read, not a single-stock event. Signal: the market's grading rubric is now explicit across all three big-tech reports this week — cash conversion and guidance beat revenue growth. Alphabet (-$9.07B FCF), Amazon (-$42.4B TTM FCF) and even beat-and-raise Microsoft are all being read through that lens, and guidance softness is being punished even on beats (Reddit -21%, Pinterest -12%). Noise: Thursday's breadth held up (9 of 11 sectors green, advancers ahead, Russell +1.01%, equal-weight S&P +1.20%) and energy is offsetting, so this remains a concentrated megacap-tech de-risking, not broad risk-off — which is exactly why the 8:30 a.m. ET Employment Cost Index matters: a hot print would feed the ~75% December-hike pricing and could turn a tech rotation into a market-wide one.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Fresh this hour: ExxonMobil and Chevron both beat Q3 profit expectations on a war-driven refining surge — Exxon earned more from refining than upstream for the first time in at least six years; Exxon adjusted EPS $4.23, Chevron $5.28. Shares +2% and +1% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy is the morning's confirmed offset — strong oil-major prints reinforce the rotation out of tech and keep the Dow near flat while Nasdaq futures sink.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a tech-led soft open: Nasdaq 100 futures -2.33% (-687 points), S&P 500 futures -1.04%, Dow futures +0.03% as Amazon and Intel earnings deepen Thursday's tech selloff.
headlines.why_it_matters: A concentrated tech open, not broad risk-off — the Dow near flat shows the pressure is in megacap tech and chips, not the whole market.

headlines.headline: Amazon falls ~7.2% premarket after Q3 missed: net sales $201.9B vs ~$202.3B expected, EPS $1.89 vs ~$1.96-1.97 expected, despite AWS +39% to $46.0B (fastest in nearly five years) and a record 13.9% operating margin. Trailing-12-month free cash flow swung to -$42.4B from +$14.8B a year earlier on $77.3B of quarterly property/equipment spending; 2026 cash capex held at ~$220B, with AWS growth projected above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Q4 sales guide of $240-247B has a midpoint below the ~$244.5B consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even a record margin and accelerating AWS could not offset the cash line — the market is grading AI spenders on free cash flow, and Amazon just joined Alphabet on the wrong side of that test.

headlines.headline: Intel plunges ~25-26% premarket despite a Q3 beat: revenue $16.5B (+21% y/y), adjusted EPS $0.52 vs ~$0.41 expected, data-center/AI +78% to $7.3B — but Q4 guidance of $15-16B revenue and $0.25 EPS trails the ~$17.1-17.3B / $0.43-0.45 consensus, client computing fell 5% to $8.1B, adjusted gross margin guided to 38% from 44.1%, and the company warned the PC market declines into at least H1 2027 with an Israel fab explosion costing ~$300M per quarter.
headlines.why_it_matters: A demand warning from Intel hits the whole chip complex — AMD -8.6%, Broadcom -3.8% and Nvidia -2.9% premarket, plus Dell and HP falling, so this is a sector read, not just one stock.

headlines.headline: Alphabet steadies after Thursday's rout: GOOGL fell 12.64% Thursday to $283.82, its worst day since its 2004 IPO, on the Q3 miss (revenue $127.58B vs ~$128.2B expected, EPS $2.12 vs ~$2.94) and -$9.07B free cash flow; premarket Friday it was only about -0.4% to -0.7%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bleeding has paused, not reversed — Alphabet is no longer the day's driver, but its Thursday repricing set the bar Amazon and Intel then failed.

headlines.headline: Megacap premarket snapshot (Finnhub, ~07:49-07:54 ET): Meta -1.87% to $612.83, Microsoft -0.65% to $526.67 — both lower, with Meta still sliding after its $95B equity raise announcement and Ackman's CNBC defense calling it 'incredibly undervalued.'
headlines.why_it_matters: Even Thursday's winners and vocal defenders are being pulled in — Microsoft's cash-backed beat is no longer an offset when the whole tech complex is de-risking into the open.

headlines.headline: After-hours selloff spread beyond the megacaps: Reddit -21.7% premarket after beating Q3 ($1.40 EPS on $895M revenue) but guiding Q4 revenue of $1.00-1.03B vs ~$1.05B consensus, with CEO warning daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if search referrals keep declining; Pinterest fell ~12% after missing Q3.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance is punishing growth names across the board — beats are being sold when the outlook softens, which widens the open's drag beyond the index heavyweights.

headlines.headline: Prior session (Thu Oct 29) hid a rotation: S&P 500 -0.30% to 7,720.39, Nasdaq -1.38% to 26,184.72, Dow -0.25% to 52,342.56 — but 9 of 11 sectors rose, advancers outnumbered decliners on both exchanges, the Russell 2000 gained 1.01% to 2,859.22, and the equal-weight S&P rose 1.20% while the cap-weighted index fell. 10-year yield ended near 4.98%, WTI near $103.37, gold near $4,004, bitcoin near $78,134.
headlines.why_it_matters: The headline declines overstate the damage — breadth held up Thursday, so today's question is whether the Amazon/Intel leg finally breaks that rotation or stays contained in tech.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. Q3 earnings land before the open Tue Nov 3 (11 a.m. ET call) and the $0.525 Q3 distribution ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Oil rebounding premarket (WTI ~$103.52, +1.49%) and the Exxon/Chevron refining beats keep a supportive energy backdrop, with no company-specific catalyst ahead of Nov 3.
